biography.plain_text: Bill McEachnie is a Canadian forester and log broker associated with S.A. Mowat in British Columbia. Now retired, he has supported charitable fundraising with his wife, Katherine, a wine educator. Their activities have included the Vancouver International Wine Festival and support for community organisations in the Okanagan, including Agur Lake Camp.

long_biography.plain_text:
Forestry businessman Bill McEachnie took an organising role in Vancouver's Hoo-Hoo Club, part of an international association for the forest-products industry. He chaired its membership committee and served as a director. Working with fellow members Ed Reid and Colin Jensen, he helped prepare a wine-and-cheese gathering at the Coach House Motor Inn.

An auction purchase gave him a way to support forest education. In 2006, he made the winning bid for Andrea Levasseur's watercolour of Evans Lake. He planned to have it framed and give it to the Evans Lake Forest Education Centre for display at the camp, the club's principal fundraising beneficiary.
